content.adv-fajr-alarm.endings.one_prayer.whatHa: Fajr stays hard. Isha becomes theirs — every night, together.
content.adv-fajr-alarm.endings.one_prayer.patter: Instead of fighting over the hardest prayer, they found an easier one to share.
content.adv-fajr-alarm.endings.one_prayer.takeaw: Start where it is easy to meet.
We pray at least one prayer together each day.
content.adv-fajr-alarm.endings.own_pace.title: At their own pace
content.adv-fajr-alarm.endings.own_pace.image.al: Zaid and Amal walking at their own pace.
content.adv-fajr-alarm.endings.own_pace.whatHapp: Not resolved, not broken. Two people at different places, learning not to measure each other.
Spouses rarely grow at the same speed; the question is how they treat the gap.
content.adv-fajr-alarm.endings.own_pace.takeaway: Your spouse’s journey is theirs. Your patience is yours.
content.adv-fajr-alarm.endings.own_pace.epilogue: Some unspoken pressure still hangs over the alarm clock.
content.adv-fajr-alarm.endings.own_pace.guide.fa: We give each other room to grow at our own pace.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.title: The Mahr Conversation
content.adv-mahr-conversation.tagline: Two fathers, one number, and a bride nobody has asked.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.description: Faris and Layla are newly engaged. Her father names a mahr his family finds insulting; his father names one hers finds insulting back. Play both of them through the week the families negotiate — and decide whether the couple has a voice in their own beginning.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.cover.alt: Two fathers in tense conversation while the couple watch.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.roles.A.name: Faris
content.adv-mahr-conversation.roles.A.sketch: A teacher; respects his father, has modest savings.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.roles.B.name: Layla
content.adv-mahr-conversation.roles.B.sketch: A pharmacist; knows exactly what the mahr means to her.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.variables.partners: They are watching their families decide.
They are finding their voice together.
They are deciding as a couple.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.variables.voice.re: Layla’s own wishes led the decision.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.figures.ima: The two fathers naming figures in the living room.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.figures.pas: The first formal visit. Layla’s father names a mahr. The room goes quiet. Faris’s father names a much smaller one. The room goes colder.
Nobody has asked Layla. Nobody has asked Faris what he can actually afford.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.figures.dec: You are Faris. What do you do in the room?
“With respect — could we hear what Layla would like?”
Faris asked, in front of both families, what Layla wanted.
The mahr is the bride’s right. Asking her is not rudeness — it is the point.
Stay quiet — this is for the elders.
Faris stayed quiet and let the elders talk.
Back his father: “We have to be realistic.”
Faris backed his father’s figure in the room.
Layla looking at her phone on the drive home.
In the car, Layla’s mother is furious. Layla’s phone buzzes: Faris.
She is still a little stunned that he asked what she wanted.
You are Layla. What do you do?
Call Faris tonight: “We need to talk, just us.”
Layla called Faris that night so they could talk alone.
Let her mother vent, and agree with everything.
Layla let her mother’s anger set the tone.
Text: “I don’t care about the number. I care that nobody asked me.”
Layla told Faris what hurt was not the number but not being asked.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.fathers_mee: The two fathers meeting alone at a café.
Without telling the couple, the two fathers meet to “settle it like men”. Faris hears about it afterwards.
You are Faris. What do you do?
Tell his father: “Layla and I will settle the mahr together.”
Faris told his father the couple would settle the mahr themselves.
Faris accepted whatever the fathers agreed.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.just_us.ima: Faris and Layla talking on a video call.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.just_us.pas: For the first time, they talk about the mahr without anyone else in the room.
Layla explains that what stung was being spoken about, not spoken to.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.just_us.dec: What does the mahr mean to you? Answer for yourself.
An honour I want to give properly — even if it takes time.
Faris said the mahr was an honour he wanted to give properly.
Honestly, a worry: I can only afford so much.
Faris admitted what he could actually afford.
A formality our families care about more than we do.
Faris called the mahr a formality for the families.
My right — and I want to choose it myself.
Layla said the mahr was her right to choose.
A symbol. Something meaningful matters more than the amount.
Layla said a meaningful mahr mattered more than its size.
Security, for a future I can’t predict.
Layla said the mahr was about security.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.leak.title: The aunties hear
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.leak.passag: An aunt has told half the community both families’ figures. Messages arrive: “Is it true they’re haggling over you?”
The figure the fathers agreed is now public — and Layla learns it from her cousin.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.leak.decisi: You are Layla. How do you respond?
Call Faris: “Let’s answer this together, once, and then say nothing.”
Layla asked Faris to face the gossip together.
Layla wondered aloud whether the engagement should go ahead.
Mute every group and let the families handle it.
Layla muted the groups and left it to the families.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.pause.title: A pause
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.pause.image: Faris alone on a park bench.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.pause.passa: Layla’s message sits on Faris’s screen: “Maybe this isn’t meant to be.”
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.pause.decis: You are Faris. What do you do?
Ask to meet with both mothers present and listen.
Faris asked to meet, with both mothers present, just to listen.
Suggest they both pray istikhara and talk in a week.
Faris suggested they both pray istikhara before deciding.
“If that’s what you want, I understand.”
Faris accepted it without a fight.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.decide_toge: Layla speaking while the families listen.
Whatever happens next, Faris and Layla agree it will be decided with them in the room.
Both prayed istikhara this week. They feel calmer than their families.
Together: how is the mahr decided?
Layla names it; Faris says honestly what he can give now and later.
Layla named the mahr, and Faris was honest about now and later.
A meaningful mahr — a set of things chosen together, not a number.
They chose a meaningful mahr together instead of a number.
Meet the fathers halfway to keep the peace.
They split the difference between the fathers.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.scenes.tell_father: Faris and Layla telling their fathers.
They go to both fathers together.
You are Faris. How do you put it?
“We’ve decided together, and we’d love your blessing.”
Faris told the fathers the couple had decided and asked for their blessing.
“This is our decision. Please respect it.”
Faris told the fathers firmly it was the couple’s decision.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.her_mahr.i: Faris and Layla at their nikah.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.her_mahr.w: At the nikah, the imam reads out a mahr Layla chose herself. Both fathers nod.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.her_mahr.p: Families were honoured but not handed the decision.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.her_mahr.c: Nothing big — though asking Layla on the first night would have saved a week.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.her_mahr.t: The mahr is the bride’s right; the decision is the couple’s to make, with families blessing it.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.her_mahr.e: The two fathers end the evening laughing together.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.her_mahr.g: Big decisions about our marriage are made with us in the room.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.meaningful: A box holding a Qur’an, a letter and a bracelet.
The mahr is a Qur’an, a letter, and a promise of Umrah together. Layla says it is the richest thing she owns.
Talking about what the mahr meant dissolved the fight about how much.
Ask what something means before arguing about what it costs.
We talk about what things mean before what they cost.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.fathers_de: The fathers shaking hands while Layla stands apart.
The fathers shook hands on a figure. The wedding goes ahead. Layla never quite forgets that she found out from her cousin.
A decision about the bride was made without the bride.
Faris telling his father: “Layla and I will settle this together.”
Peace bought by excluding your spouse is borrowed against your marriage.
Neither of us lets family decide over the other’s head.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.compromise: Both families at the engagement gathering.
Nobody got what they wanted; everybody can live with it. The wedding is back on track.
Splitting the difference protected the families more than it expressed the couple.
Asking what each figure meant before splitting it.
Compromise is good — once you know what each side actually needs.
Before we compromise, we ask what each of us actually needs.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.stronger.i: Faris and Layla walking through a market together.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.stronger.w: The week was ugly. But Faris and Layla now know how they handle pressure: together.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.stronger.p: An early conflict with family became practice for marriage.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.stronger.c: Less of the family drama — but not the way they faced it.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.stronger.t: How you face the first family pressure sets the pattern for the rest.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.stronger.g: We face family pressure side by side, never against each other.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.bruised.im: Two mothers not speaking at the engagement dinner.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.bruised.wh: The engagement survives. The two families barely speak at the wedding.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.bruised.pa: The couple asserted themselves — but bluntly, and the families felt dismissed.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.bruised.co: The same decision, delivered with a request for blessing.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.bruised.ta: Firm and respectful are not opposites.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.bruised.gu: We can disagree with our parents and still honour them.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.apart.what: The engagement ends quietly. Both later say it was the right decision, made for the wrong reasons.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.apart.patt: Exhaustion with the families ended something the couple never really discussed.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.apart.coul: One honest conversation between the two of them, before deciding.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.apart.take: Do not let a family conflict make a decision that belongs to the two of you.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.apart.guid: We talk directly before making any big decision about us.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.numbers.wh: A figure is agreed and the nikah goes ahead. Neither of them is sure what it meant.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.numbers.pa: They got through it without ever talking about why it mattered.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.numbers.co: Talking about what the mahr meant to each of them.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.numbers.ta: Rituals you do not discuss can feel empty, even when they go smoothly.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.numbers.ep: Layla still wonders whether Faris thinks it was a formality.
content.adv-mahr-conversation.endings.numbers.gu: We talk about why our traditions matter to each of us.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.title: Three in the Morning
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.tagline: A six-week-old, two tired parents, and opinions from both grandmothers.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.description: Ibrahim and Ruqayya have a six-week-old daughter and have not slept properly since. Each quietly believes they do more. Play both of them through the nights, the visits and the first evening alone — and see whether exhaustion makes them a team or a tally.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.cover.alt: Exhausted new parents in the kitchen at 3am.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.roles.A.name: Ibrahim
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.roles.A.sketch: Back at work after two weeks; feels useless at night.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.roles.B.name: Ruqayya
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.roles.B.sketch: Feeding every two hours; feels invisible by day.
They are coping side by side.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.variables.resen: A lot is being counted in silence.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.cry.imag: Ruqayya sitting up with the crying baby at night.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.cry.pass: The baby is crying again. It is the fourth time tonight. Ibrahim has work at eight.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.cry.deci: You are Ibrahim. What do you do?
Get up, change her, and bring her to Ruqayya to feed.
Ibrahim got up at three to change the baby.
Pretend to be asleep. Ruqayya’s up anyway.
She almost certainly noticed. What she noticed is now a story she tells herself.
Whisper: “Shall I take the next one?”
Ibrahim offered to take the next waking.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.breakfas: Ibrahim leaving for work as Ruqayya holds the baby.
Ibrahim is grabbing his keys. Ruqayya has not showered in two days.
She heard him pretending to sleep.
You are Ruqayya. What do you say?
“Can you take her for an hour when you’re home? I need a shower and a nap.”
Ruqayya asked plainly for an hour to herself.
“Must be nice, going to work and talking to adults.”
Ruqayya made a pointed remark about Ibrahim going to work.
Ruqayya said nothing and coped alone.
Two grandmothers giving advice to Ruqayya.
Both grandmothers arrive with food and opinions. Ibrahim’s mother says the baby is “too hot”. Ruqayya’s mother says she should be feeding differently.
You are Ibrahim. What do you do?
“Ruqayya knows her best. Shall I make everyone tea?”
Ibrahim backed Ruqayya in front of both grandmothers.
Give the grandmothers jobs: cooking and laundry, not advice.
Ibrahim gave the grandmothers practical jobs instead of advice.
Agree with his mother — she raised five children.
Ibrahim agreed with his mother’s advice in front of Ruqayya.
Ibrahim and Ruqayya on the sofa, the baby asleep between them.
The baby sleeps. Both of them are too tired to talk, and too wound up not to.
Weeks of silence are sitting on Ruqayya’s chest.
Mention everything he has done this week.
Ibrahim listed what he had done that week.
Ibrahim asked Ruqayya how she really was.
Ibrahim scrolled his phone to decompress.
Ruqayya admitted she was not okay.
Point out how many nights she has done alone.
Ruqayya pointed out how many nights she had done alone.
Go to bed without a word.
Ruqayya went to bed without a word.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.scorecar: A notepad of tally marks on the kitchen counter.
A week later, they are keeping count — out loud. Nights, nappies, hours.
You are Ruqayya. What do you do?
“We’re on the same side. Can we stop counting?”
Ruqayya asked them to stop keeping count.
Move in with her mother for a week.
Ruqayya went to stay with her mother for a week.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.night_pl: Ibrahim and Ruqayya planning the nights in a notebook.
They sit down with a notebook and try to plan the nights.
Ruqayya is back from her mother’s. It is awkward, but they are talking.
You both need to choose the same plan.
Together: how will the nights work?
Shifts: he takes 10–2, she takes 2–6, with expressed milk.
They split the nights into shifts.
He takes every weekend night, so she gets two full sleeps.
Ask a grandmother to stay over twice a week.
They asked a grandmother to stay over twice a week.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.first_ev: Ibrahim and Ruqayya on their first evening out.
Eight weeks in. A grandmother has the baby. They are at a restaurant, alone, for the first time since the birth.
What do you want from tonight?
To talk about us — not the baby.
One of them wanted to talk about the two of them.
To check the monitor and go home early.
One of them wanted to check in and go home early.
To finally say the hard things.
One of them wanted to finally say the hard things.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.month.im: Ibrahim playing with the baby as Ruqayya watches.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.month.pa: Three months. The baby smiles now. The question is what kind of parents — and spouses — they have become.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.scenes.month.de: You are Ibrahim. What do you say to Ruqayya?
“I don’t know how you did those first weeks. Thank you.”
Ibrahim thanked Ruqayya for those first weeks.
Ibrahim decided the worst was over and said nothing.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.team.im: Ibrahim and Ruqayya pushing the pram through a park.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.team.wh: The nights are still hard. But they are hard together.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.team.pa: They turned exhaustion into a joint problem instead of a contest.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.team.co: Nothing big; asking “how are you really?” sooner.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.team.ta: In the newborn months, ask how your spouse is before you say what you did.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.team.ep: Their shifts system becomes family legend.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.team.gu: We are on the same side, especially when we are exhausted.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.tally.i: Ibrahim and Ruqayya passing the baby without eye contact.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.tally.w: They parent efficiently and talk about little else. The tally never really stopped.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.tally.p: Each kept proof of doing more, so neither felt seen.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.tally.c: Saying “I’m not okay” instead of “I did more”.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.tally.t: Nobody wins a tally. Both lose the marriage behind it.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.tally.g: We do not keep score; we say what we need.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.village: A grandmother rocking the baby while the couple sleep.
With grandmothers doing jobs instead of giving advice, everyone sleeps a little more.
Family help works when it serves the couple’s plan.
Setting those roles from week one.
Ask family for help with tasks, not decisions.
We welcome family help for tasks; decisions stay ours.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.seen.im: Ibrahim hugging Ruqayya as she holds the baby.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.seen.wh: The night she admitted she was not okay, something changed. She stopped carrying it alone.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.seen.pa: Saying “I’m not okay” opened the door that coping kept shut.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.seen.ta: Coping in silence is not strength; it is distance.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.seen.ep: They still use the shifts they planned that week.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.seen.gu: We tell each other when we are not okay.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.apart_h: Ibrahim alone in the empty nursery.
She comes back after a week. They are polite. Something has to be rebuilt.
Leaving relieved the pressure without fixing what caused it.
One honest night-plan conversation before she left.
Space can help — if you agree why you are taking it and when you will talk.
If we need space, we say why and when we will talk.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.weekend: Ibrahim feeding the baby at sunrise.
Ibrahim’s weekend nights become his time with his daughter — and Ruqayya’s two full sleeps a week.
A simple, owned task stopped the vague sense of unfairness.
A clear job each beats a vague promise to “help”.
A grandmother still drops by with food every Friday.
We each own clear jobs rather than “helping” each other.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.unspoke: Ibrahim and Ruqayya smiling for a photo at the first birthday.
They got through the first year. Ruqayya still thinks about the nights she did alone.
What was never said stayed, quietly, after the hard months ended.
Ibrahim saying thank you, and Ruqayya saying what it cost.
Name what the hard season cost each of you, even after it ends.
We thank each other out loud for the hard seasons.
content.adv-three-in-the-morning.endings.getting: Ibrahim and Ruqayya sharing late-night noodles on the stairs.
Some good nights, some bad. They are still learning how to be parents and spouses at once.
Every couple is clumsy in the newborn months; what matters is noticing.
A clearer plan for the nights.
Plan the nights before you are too tired to plan anything.
Some tallies are still being kept quietly.
We plan hard seasons together before they start.
content.adv-public-private.title: Public Couple, Private Couple
content.adv-public-private.tagline: She posts their life. He wants it kept between them. Then a post goes viral.
content.adv-public-private.description: Rania has a growing following for her calm, faith-centred lifestyle posts — and their marriage is part of it. Tariq is a private man who never agreed to be content. Play both of them through a sponsorship offer, a viral post about their first argument, and the comment section that follows.
content.adv-public-private.cover.alt: A wife filming coffees while her husband hides behind a menu.
content.adv-public-private.roles.A.name: Tariq
content.adv-public-private.roles.A.sketch: An accountant; quiet, loyal, allergic to attention.
content.adv-public-private.roles.B.name: Rania
content.adv-public-private.roles.B.sketch: Shares modest-lifestyle content to 40,000 followers; it pays.
content.adv-public-private.variables.trust.label: Trust
content.adv-public-private.variables.closeness.r: They feel like a brand and its subject.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.sponsor.title: The offer
Rania showing Tariq a sponsorship email.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.sponsor.passag: A modest-fashion brand wants Rania for a paid campaign: “couple content”, six posts, both of them on camera.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.sponsor.decisi: You are Rania. What do you do?
Show Tariq and ask how he feels before replying.
Rania asked Tariq how he felt before replying to the brand.
Say yes — he’ll come round, and the money is good.
Rania accepted the campaign before asking Tariq.
Counter-offer: she’ll do it alone, no husband.
Rania offered to do the campaign without Tariq.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.reaction.title: Tariq hears
content.adv-public-private.scenes.reaction.image: Tariq considering his answer at the kitchen table.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.reaction.decis: You are Tariq. What do you say?
“I’ll support your work. But I want us to agree what’s off-limits.”
Tariq offered support on condition they agreed limits together.
“I never agreed to be part of this. No.”
Tariq refused to be part of it at all.
“Fine.” He doesn’t want to be the reason she loses money.
Tariq went along with it to avoid an argument.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.argument.title: The first real argument
content.adv-public-private.scenes.argument.image: Tariq and Rania arguing beside her ring light.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.argument.passa: A week later, a real argument — about chores, about the campaign, about everything. Rania, upset, writes a vague, emotional post: “When marriage gets hard, keep showing up.” It is clearly about them.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.argument.lesso: Posting about a conflict — even vaguely — invites strangers into it.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.argument.decis: You are Rania. Do you post it?
Post it. It’s honest, and it might help someone.
Keep it in drafts and talk to Tariq first.
Rania kept the post in drafts and talked to Tariq first.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.viral.title: It goes viral
content.adv-public-private.scenes.viral.image.al: Tariq at work seeing the viral post.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.viral.passages: The post goes viral. 300,000 views. Strangers speculate about their marriage. Tariq’s colleagues have seen it.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.viral.decision: Call Rania: “Can we talk tonight? I’m not angry, I’m exposed.”
Tariq called Rania to say he felt exposed, not angry.
Go cold. Say nothing until she notices.
Tariq went cold and waited for her to notice.
Take it down and call Tariq.
Rania took the post down and called Tariq.
Leave it up — the engagement is good for her account.
Rania left the post up for the engagement.
Post a follow-up saying they’re fine.
Rania posted a follow-up saying they were fine.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.comments.title: The comment section
content.adv-public-private.scenes.comments.image: Rania reading comments late at night.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.comments.passa: The comments turn: some say Tariq sounds controlling, others say Rania is exploiting her marriage.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.comments.decis: You are Tariq. Rania is hurting. What do you do?
Sit with her, take her phone gently, and make tea.
Tariq sat with Rania and gently took her phone away.
“This is exactly what I was worried about.”
Tariq told Rania this was what he had warned about.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.boundaries.ima: Tariq and Rania listing what stays private.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.boundaries.pas: They finally talk about what is shareable and what is theirs alone.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.boundaries.les: Choose together. A mismatch means talk, then choose again.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.boundaries.dec: Together: what’s the rule from now on?
Never post about conflict, and Tariq approves any post he’s in.
They agreed never to post conflict, and Tariq approves any post he is in.
Rania keeps creating — but Tariq is never on camera.
They agreed Tariq would stay off camera entirely.
Make the account private for a while.
They agreed to make the account private for a while.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.campaign.title: The campaign
content.adv-public-private.scenes.campaign.image: Rania filming while Tariq reads out of frame.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.campaign.passa: The brand is still waiting for an answer about the campaign.
The account is private now. The brand is not thrilled.
content.adv-public-private.scenes.campaign.decis: You are Rania. What do you tell the brand?
Do it alone, on her terms.
Rania did the campaign alone, on her terms.
Decline. It isn’t worth what it costs at home.
Rania declined the campaign for the sake of home.
Do the couple content anyway — one last time.
Rania did the couple content anyway.
content.adv-public-private.endings.protected.ima: Tariq and Rania laughing at a picnic, phones away.
content.adv-public-private.endings.protected.wha: Rania’s work thrives; their marriage stays off it. Tariq has started helping with her editing.
content.adv-public-private.endings.protected.pat: Clear, shared rules let one spouse’s public life and the other’s privacy coexist.
content.adv-public-private.endings.protected.cou: Agreeing those rules before the first sponsored post.
content.adv-public-private.endings.protected.tak: Decide together what belongs to the public and what belongs to you.
content.adv-public-private.endings.protected.epi: Her followers notice she seems calmer. She is.
content.adv-public-private.endings.protected.gui: We agree together what we share online, and never post our conflicts.
content.adv-public-private.endings.offscreen.ima: Tariq’s hand passing Rania tea, just out of frame.
content.adv-public-private.endings.offscreen.wha: Her followers know she is married. They never see him. He likes it that way; so does she, eventually.
content.adv-public-private.endings.offscreen.pat: Each kept what mattered to them without forcing the other.
content.adv-public-private.endings.offscreen.cou: Starting there — before the brand ever asked.
content.adv-public-private.endings.offscreen.tak: A spouse’s privacy is theirs to choose, not yours to spend.
content.adv-public-private.endings.offscreen.gui: Neither of us shares the other online without asking.
content.adv-public-private.endings.quiet.title: The quiet season
content.adv-public-private.endings.quiet.image.a: Tariq and Rania on a balcony, phone face down.
content.adv-public-private.endings.quiet.whatHap: The account stays private for six months. Rania misses it, then doesn’t. They feel like themselves again.
content.adv-public-private.endings.quiet.pattern: Pausing the public life gave the private one room to heal.
content.adv-public-private.endings.quiet.couldHa: A smaller step might have kept her income.
content.adv-public-private.endings.quiet.takeawa: Sometimes protecting the marriage means a quieter season.
content.adv-public-private.endings.quiet.guide.p: If something outside starts hurting us, we pause it.
content.adv-public-private.endings.exposed.title: Exposed
content.adv-public-private.endings.exposed.image: Tariq alone with a couple photo on his phone.
content.adv-public-private.endings.exposed.whatH: The couple content went live. Tariq is polite. He has stopped telling Rania anything personal.
content.adv-public-private.endings.exposed.patte: One spouse’s comfort became the other’s product.
content.adv-public-private.endings.exposed.could: Asking him first — and taking no for an answer.
content.adv-public-private.endings.exposed.takea: Trust is the one thing you cannot monetise.
content.adv-public-private.endings.exposed.guide: We never trade the other’s privacy for anything.
content.adv-public-private.endings.engagement.im: Rania filming while Tariq leaves the room behind her.
content.adv-public-private.endings.engagement.wh: The viral post stayed up and the account doubled. The marriage feels thinner.
content.adv-public-private.endings.engagement.pa: The approval of strangers outweighed the one person who mattered.
content.adv-public-private.endings.engagement.co: Taking it down the moment he said he felt exposed.
content.adv-public-private.endings.engagement.ta: Strangers’ attention is loud; your spouse’s hurt is quiet. Listen to the quiet one.
content.adv-public-private.endings.engagement.gu: When one of us feels exposed, the post comes down.
content.adv-public-private.endings.together.imag: Tariq and Rania close on the sofa, phone switched off.
content.adv-public-private.endings.together.what: The worst week of her online life was the week he showed up most. She has not forgotten.
content.adv-public-private.endings.together.patt: He chose comfort over being right when she was hurting.
content.adv-public-private.endings.together.coul: Not posting about the argument in the first place.
content.adv-public-private.endings.together.take: When your spouse is hurting, comfort first; “I told you so” never.
content.adv-public-private.endings.together.guid: When one of us is hurting, we comfort first and talk later.
content.adv-public-private.endings.compromise.im: Tariq and Rania reviewing photos together.
content.adv-public-private.endings.compromise.wh: They are still negotiating what is shareable, post by post. It is slow, but it is together.
content.adv-public-private.endings.compromise.pa: Clear rules were not set, but the habit of asking was.
content.adv-public-private.endings.compromise.co: A written agreement would save them some arguments.
content.adv-public-private.endings.compromise.ta: Asking each time is good; agreeing the rules once is better.
content.adv-public-private.endings.compromise.ep: The viral week still comes up in arguments.
content.adv-public-private.endings.compromise.gu: We ask before posting anything about us.
content.adv-public-private.endings.cold.title: Cold war, online and off
content.adv-public-private.endings.cold.image.al: Tariq and Rania on their phones at opposite ends of the sofa.
content.adv-public-private.endings.cold.whatHapp: Neither apologised. Rania posts less. They talk even less.
Both protected themselves and left the marriage unprotected.
content.adv-public-private.endings.cold.couldHav: One of them reaching out on the night of the viral post.
content.adv-public-private.endings.cold.takeaway: Silence after a public hurt only makes it private and permanent.
content.adv-public-private.endings.cold.guide.pp: After a hurt, one of us reaches out within a day.
content.adv-upstairs-room.title: The Upstairs Room
content.adv-upstairs-room.tagline: One room, no lock, and a mother-in-law with a key to everything.
content.adv-upstairs-room.description: To save for a deposit, Yahya and Sumaya move into the upstairs room at his parents’ house. It was meant to be a year. Play both of them through overheard conversations, kitchen politics and a moving-out date that keeps slipping — and decide what a couple needs to stay a couple under someone else’s roof.
content.adv-upstairs-room.cover.alt: A family staircase leading to the couple’s room.
content.adv-upstairs-room.roles.A.name: Yahya
content.adv-upstairs-room.roles.A.sketch: An only son; grateful to his parents, conflict-averse.
content.adv-upstairs-room.roles.B.name: Sumaya
content.adv-upstairs-room.roles.B.sketch: Independent; agreed to the plan for the deposit, and is starting to feel like a guest.
content.adv-upstairs-room.variables.privacy.read: They have no space of their own.
Their marriage has a protected corner.
content.adv-upstairs-room.variables.family.label: Family warmth
Sumaya feels alone in the house.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.knock.title: The knock that isn’t
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.knock.image.alt: Yahya’s mother walking in with laundry.
Week three. Yahya’s mother walks into their room with folded laundry — without knocking — for the fourth time.
You are Sumaya. What do you do?
Tell Yahya that evening and ask him to raise it.
Sumaya asked Yahya to raise the knocking with his mother.
Say to his mother kindly: “Could you knock first? I’m not always dressed.”
Sumaya asked her mother-in-law directly to knock.
Sumaya said nothing because it was their house.
Feeling like a guest in your own marriage is a small thing that grows.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.yahya_mum.title: A word with Mum
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.yahya_mum.image: Yahya talking with his mother in the kitchen.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.yahya_mum.passa: Yahya finds his mother in the kitchen. He hates this.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.yahya_mum.decis: You are Yahya. How do you put it?
“Mum, could you knock on our door? It matters to me.”
Yahya asked his mother to knock, as his own request.
Yahya told his mother the request came from Sumaya.
Passing on a request as your spouse’s puts them between you and your parent.
Chat about dinner and lose his nerve.
Yahya lost his nerve and never raised it.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.kitchen.title: Whose kitchen
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.kitchen.image.a: Sumaya and her mother-in-law in the kitchen.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.kitchen.passage: Sumaya cooks dinner for the family. Her mother-in-law quietly re-seasons it.
Since the knocking conversation, things have been chilly.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.kitchen.decisio: You are Sumaya. What do you do?
Suggest they cook together on Fridays.
Sumaya suggested cooking together on Fridays.
Stop cooking. Let her run the kitchen.
Sumaya stopped cooking and left the kitchen to her mother-in-law.
Mention to Yahya, without drama, that it stung.
Sumaya told Yahya calmly that the re-seasoning stung.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.overheard.title: Through the wall
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.overheard.image: Yahya and Sumaya overhearing through the wall.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.overheard.passa: Late at night, through the wall: his father saying, “When are they actually leaving? She acts like a guest.”
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.overheard.decis: What do you do, in that moment?
Take Sumaya’s hand: “I heard it too. We’ll talk tomorrow.”
Yahya took Sumaya’s hand and said they would talk tomorrow.
Whisper: “He didn’t mean it like that.”
Yahya pretended he had not heard.
Sumaya said they needed to leave soon.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.savings.title: The savings account
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.savings.image.a: Yahya and Sumaya looking at their savings.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.savings.passage: They look at the savings. Eight months in, they are behind — Yahya has been quietly paying some of his parents’ bills.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.savings.decisio: You are Yahya. How do you tell her?
Tell her plainly, and ask how she feels about it.
Yahya told Sumaya plainly about paying his parents’ bills.
“They’re my parents. What was I supposed to do?”
Yahya defended paying his parents’ bills without asking her.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.deadline.title: A date on the calendar
A move-out date circled on the calendar.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.deadline.passag: Sumaya has already said it: they need to leave soon.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.deadline.lesson: Choose together; if you differ, talk and choose again.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.deadline.decisi: Set a firm moving-out date in six months, and tell his parents together.
They set a firm move-out date and agreed to tell his parents together.
Stay longer, but agree house rules with his parents.
They chose to stay longer with agreed house rules.
Rent a small flat now, even if the deposit takes longer.
They chose to rent a small flat right away.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.tell_parents.im: Yahya and Sumaya talking with his parents.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.tell_parents.pa: They sit down with his parents in the living room.
content.adv-upstairs-room.scenes.tell_parents.de: You are Yahya. How do you begin?
“We’re so grateful for this year. Here’s what we’ve decided, together.”
Yahya began with gratitude and spoke for them both.
Let Sumaya explain — it’s mostly her wish.
Yahya let Sumaya explain the decision alone.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.own_door.title: Their own front door
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.own_door.image: Yahya and Sumaya at their own front door.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.own_door.whatH: Six months later they carry the last box out. His parents cry, then come for Friday dinner every week.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.own_door.patte: They left as a team, with gratitude, so leaving did not feel like rejection.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.own_door.could: Setting the date on day one.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.own_door.takea: Gratitude and boundaries can be said in the same breath.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.own_door.guide: We speak to our families as one, with gratitude first.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.rules.title: House rules
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.rules.image.al: His mother knocking politely on their door.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.rules.whatHapp: They stay another year. His mother knocks now. Fridays, the two women cook together.
Clear rules made a shared house livable.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.rules.takeaway: Living with family works best with rules agreed before the first problem.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.rules.epilogue: Sumaya still counts the days until they move — but without bitterness.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.rules.guide.ur: If we share a home with family, we agree house rules first.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.small_flat.tit: A small flat, a big relief
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.small_flat.ima: Yahya and Sumaya eating takeaway on the floor of a tiny flat.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.small_flat.wha: The deposit takes two more years. They don’t regret it for a day.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.small_flat.pat: They decided their privacy was worth more than speed.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.small_flat.cou: Telling his parents more warmly would have eased the hurt.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.small_flat.epi: His parents take a while to forgive the speed of it.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.small_flat.gui: We weigh our marriage’s needs alongside our savings.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.guest.title: A guest in her marriage
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.guest.image.al: Sumaya alone, suitcase still half unpacked.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.guest.whatHapp: Two years on, they still live upstairs. Sumaya has never unpacked the second suitcase.
Each small thing was endured, and the endurance became the marriage.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.guest.couldHav: Yahya speaking up — in his own voice — about the smallest thing.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.guest.takeaway: Your spouse should never feel like a guest in your marriage.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.guest.guide.ur: We make sure neither of us feels like a guest at home.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.between.title: Caught between
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.between.whatHa: Yahya relays complaints in both directions. Everyone is a little angry with him, and with each other.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.between.patter: Speaking for his wife instead of with her made him the channel for every grievance.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.between.couldH: Making requests as his own, and speaking to his parents with Sumaya beside him.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.between.takeaw: Do not be the messenger between your spouse and your parents. Be the bridge.
Requests to family come from both of us, in our own voices.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.warm_house.ima: The whole family laughing at dinner.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.warm_house.wha: Against the odds, the house becomes a real home for all four of them.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.warm_house.pat: Sumaya’s invitations and Yahya’s honesty built real warmth.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.warm_house.cou: A clearer moving-out date might still be wise.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.warm_house.tak: Warmth is built by invitations, not just boundaries.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.warm_house.gui: We build warmth with family on purpose.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.hurt_leaving.i: His parents watching them load the car.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.hurt_leaving.w: They move out. His parents feel blamed; Sumaya feels blamed for leaving.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.hurt_leaving.p: The decision was right, but Yahya let Sumaya carry it alone.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.hurt_leaving.c: Yahya standing beside her and owning the decision too.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.hurt_leaving.t: A shared decision should be defended by both of you.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.hurt_leaving.g: We both own our shared decisions in front of family.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.patience.title: Patience, for now
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.patience.image: Yahya and Sumaya talking quietly on the balcony.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.patience.whatH: They are still upstairs, still saving, still finding small ways to be a couple in a shared house.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.patience.patte: They did not fix the house, but they protected some evenings for themselves.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.patience.takea: A temporary arrangement needs a real end date.
content.adv-upstairs-room.endings.patience.guide: Temporary arrangements get a real end date.
content.adv-old-friend.title: The Old Friend
content.adv-old-friend.tagline: An old colleague asks for career advice. It is innocent. Isn’t it?
content.adv-old-friend.description: Sami’s former colleague from university starts messaging him for career advice. Nothing improper is said. Leila is not sure it feels innocent, and is not sure she is allowed to say so. Play both of them through late messages, a work dinner, and the boundaries a marriage needs.
content.adv-old-friend.cover.alt: A phone notification glowing at night beside a sleeping husband.
content.adv-old-friend.roles.A.name: Sami
content.adv-old-friend.roles.A.sketch: Helpful to a fault; does not think of himself as someone anyone needs to worry about.
content.adv-old-friend.roles.B.name: Leila
content.adv-old-friend.roles.B.sketch: Trusting, but has been hurt before by things left unsaid.
content.adv-old-friend.variables.trust.label: Trust
content.adv-old-friend.variables.security.label: Leila’s security
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.notification.title: 11:40 p.m.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.notification.image: Leila noticing a late-night message on Sami’s phone.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.notification.passa: Sami’s phone lights up at 11:40 p.m.: “Thank you so much again, you’re a lifesaver 😊” — from Hana, his old university colleague.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.notification.decis: You are Leila. What do you do?
In the morning, ask simply: “Who’s Hana?”
Leila asked Sami simply who Hana was.
Read the messages while he sleeps.
Leila read Sami’s messages while he slept.
Checking may calm the worry for a night, and adds a secret of your own.
Leila told herself it was nothing.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.sami_answers.title: “Oh, Hana?”
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.sami_answers.passa: Over breakfast, the subject comes up.
Leila already knows what the messages say: career advice, and a lot of gratitude.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.sami_answers.decis: You are Sami. How do you respond?
Hand her the phone: “Read anything you like. She’s job hunting.”
Sami offered Leila his phone and explained.
“It’s nothing — just a colleague. Don’t be silly.”
Sami told Leila not to be silly.
This response may make your partner feel dismissed — the worry is real even if the threat isn’t.
“Are you going through my phone now?”
Sami got defensive about his phone.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.dinner_invite.imag: Sami and Leila reading a dinner invitation.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.dinner_invite.pass: Hana invites Sami to a networking dinner with her new team — as a thank-you. Spouses aren’t mentioned.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.dinner_invite.deci: You are Sami. What do you do?
Say yes — if Leila comes too.
Sami accepted the dinner only if Leila came too.
Sami went to the dinner alone.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.feelings.title: What Leila feels
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.feelings.image.alt: Leila speaking honestly as Sami listens.
That night, Leila decides to say what she actually feels.
He came home from the dinner at eleven, cheerful. She has been quiet all evening.
Listen to the end, then: “That makes sense. What would help?”
Sami listened to the end and asked what would help.
Explain at length why there’s nothing to worry about.
Sami explained at length why there was nothing to worry about.
Sami said she did not trust him.
“I trust you. I just don’t like feeling like an outsider to it.”
Leila said she trusted him but felt like an outsider.
“Why does she need you at midnight?”
Leila asked why Hana needed him at midnight.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.boundaries.title: The boundary
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.boundaries.image.a: Sami and Leila agreeing boundaries, phones on the table.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.boundaries.passage: They talk about what feels right for opposite-sex friendships in their marriage.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.boundaries.lessons: Choose together. A mismatch means talk, then choose again.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.boundaries.decisio: Advice in group chats or by email only — nothing late, nothing one-to-one.
They agreed advice would only happen in groups or by email, never late.
Nothing hidden: either can see the other’s messages any time.
They agreed either could see the other’s messages.
They agreed Sami would kindly end the friendship.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.hana_again.title: Another message
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.hana_again.image.a: Sami hesitating over a new message at work.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.hana_again.passage: A month later: “Sami, quick favour — can I call you tonight? Big interview tomorrow!”
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.hana_again.decisio: You are Sami. What do you do?
Reply by email with tips, and mention it to Leila that evening.
Sami replied by email and told Leila about it.
Call — it’s a one-off — and not mention it.
Sami took the call and did not mention it.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.leila_hears.title: A year on
Sami and Leila walking by the river.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.leila_hears.passag: A year on. Leila is asked by a friend whether she ever worries about Sami.
She found the call in his history weeks later.
content.adv-old-friend.scenes.leila_hears.decisi: You are Leila. What do you say?
Leila said she never worried now.
Leila admitted she sometimes still worried.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.nothing_hidden.im: Sami and Leila cooking together, a phone face up beside them.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.nothing_hidden.wh: Leila hasn’t thought about Hana in months. Sami still helps people — in daylight, by email.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.nothing_hidden.pa: He offered openness before it was asked for, so trust grew instead of shrinking.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.nothing_hidden.co: Little; agreeing the boundary before the first late message.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.nothing_hidden.ta: Transparency offered is worth more than transparency demanded.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.nothing_hidden.ep: Hana gets the job, and sends them both a thank-you card.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.nothing_hidden.gu: We keep opposite-sex contact in the open, in daylight, and tell each other about it.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.heard.title: Heard
content.adv-old-friend.endings.heard.image.alt: Sami and Leila forehead to forehead.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.heard.whatHappene: The night he listened without defending himself is the night Leila stopped worrying.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.heard.pattern.exp: He didn’t agree there was a threat — he agreed her feeling made sense.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.heard.takeaway: Validation does not mean agreement. It means “I understand.”
content.adv-old-friend.endings.heard.guide.of-e-: When one of us feels insecure, the other listens before explaining.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.ended.title: A kind ending
content.adv-old-friend.endings.ended.image.alt: Sami typing a kind goodbye message.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.ended.whatHappene: Sami tells Hana kindly that he’ll step back. It costs him nothing he values more than Leila’s peace.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.ended.pattern.exp: An innocent friendship was ended because the marriage mattered more.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.ended.couldHaveCh: Clearer boundaries could have kept the friendship.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.ended.takeaway: Innocent and wise are not always the same thing.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.ended.guide.of-e-: We choose what protects our marriage, even when nothing is wrong.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.hidden_call.title: The call she found
content.adv-old-friend.endings.hidden_call.whatH: The call was innocent. Hiding it was not. It takes months to rebuild what one omission broke.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.hidden_call.patte: The hiding, not the call, broke the trust.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.hidden_call.could: Mentioning it that evening — or replying by email.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.hidden_call.takea: The cover-up is always worse than the thing.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.hidden_call.guide: If we would hesitate to mention it, we mention it.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.surveillance.imag: Two phones on the table, the couple not looking at each other.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.surveillance.what: Each can read the other’s phone. Neither feels any closer.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.surveillance.patt: Checking replaced the conversations that would have built real security.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.surveillance.coul: Leila saying the feeling underneath; Sami listening.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.surveillance.guid: We build trust by talking, not by checking.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.loyalty_fight.ima: Sami and Leila on opposite sides of the kitchen island.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.loyalty_fight.wha: It stopped being about Hana weeks ago. Now it is about whether either of them is on the other’s side.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.loyalty_fight.pat: An accusation met with offence turned a worry into a war.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.loyalty_fight.cou: Leila naming the feeling instead of the suspicion; Sami hearing it.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.loyalty_fight.tak: Name the feeling, not the suspicion.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.loyalty_fight.gui: We say what we feel, not what we suspect.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.quiet_worry.title: A quiet worry
content.adv-old-friend.endings.quiet_worry.image: Leila glancing at Sami’s buzzing phone.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.quiet_worry.whatH: Nothing happened. Leila still feels a small jolt whenever his phone buzzes late.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.quiet_worry.patte: A feeling buried rather than heard stays alive.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.quiet_worry.could: Leila saying it, and Sami listening without explaining.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.quiet_worry.takea: A buried worry does not go away. It waits.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.quiet_worry.guide: We say our worries out loud, even small ones.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.steady.title: Steady enough
content.adv-old-friend.endings.steady.image.alt: Sami and Leila reading together on the sofa.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.steady.whatHappen: They found a way through, a little clumsily. Both know more about what the other needs.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.steady.pattern.ex: They worked out what felt right as they went.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.steady.couldHaveC: Agreeing boundaries before anyone needed them.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.steady.takeaway: Agree your boundaries before you are tested.
They still disagree a little about what counts as “too late”.
content.adv-old-friend.endings.steady.guide.of-e: We agree boundaries before we are tested.
content.adv-background-noise.title: Background Noise
content.adv-background-noise.tagline: Not unhappy. Just busy. And she’s stopped telling him about her day.
content.adv-background-noise.description: Two years in, Ibrahim and Sumayya are fine — busy jobs, full weekends, a comfortable routine. Ibrahim has not noticed that Sumayya stopped telling him about her day. Play both of them through a forgotten anniversary, a friend who listens better, and a weekend with no phones.
content.adv-background-noise.cover.alt: A wife talking while her husband watches TV without looking.
content.adv-background-noise.roles.A.name: Ibrahim
content.adv-background-noise.roles.A.sketch: Kind, distracted, believes things are fine because nobody is arguing.
content.adv-background-noise.roles.B.name: Sumayya
content.adv-background-noise.roles.B.sketch: Notices everything; has started keeping her day to herself.
content.adv-background-noise.variables.lonelines: One of them feels a little alone.
Sumayya feels alone inside the marriage.
content.adv-background-noise.variables.effort.re: Both are choosing each other on purpose.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.bid.title: Something funny happened
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.bid.image.al: Sumayya starting a story while Ibrahim watches TV.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.bid.passages: Sumayya comes home bursting with a story about her day. Ibrahim is watching the match.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.bid.decision: You are Ibrahim. What do you do?
Pause the match and turn to face her.
Ibrahim paused the match to listen.
A story about her day is a bid for connection. Turning toward it is most of the marriage.
Ibrahim nodded without looking away from the screen.
Ibrahim asked her to tell him at half-time.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.later.title: Half-time
Sumayya messaging a friend in the bedroom.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.later.passag: Sumayya decides what to do with the story.
Half-time comes. He has forgotten to ask.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.later.decisi: You are Sumayya. What do you do?
Try again — the story is still funny.
“I feel like you don’t really hear me lately.”
Sumayya told him she felt unheard lately.
Sumayya waiting with a small cake.
It is their anniversary. Sumayya made a cake. Ibrahim is working late — he forgot.
She already told him she felt unheard. It sits in the room like a third person.
When he gets in, what happens?
See the cake, stop, and say: “I forgot. I’m so sorry. Can we sit?”
Ibrahim saw the cake and owned forgetting.
Explain about the deadline at work.
Ibrahim promised a proper celebration at the weekend.
Tell him it hurt — and that she wants this to change.
Sumayya told him it hurt and she wanted change.
Sumayya said it was fine and put the cake away.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.asma.title: A better listener
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.asma.image.a: Sumayya confiding in her friend Asma.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.asma.passage: At coffee, Sumayya’s friend Asma says, gently: “You talk to me about your day more than you talk to him, don’t you?”
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.asma.decisio: You are Sumayya. What do you do with that?
Go home and tell Ibrahim exactly what Asma noticed.
Sumayya went home and told Ibrahim what her friend had noticed.
Keep confiding in Asma. It’s easier.
Sumayya kept confiding in her friend instead of her husband.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.notices.pass: Ibrahim realises he can’t remember the last thing Sumayya told him about her day.
She has just told him, plainly, what her friend noticed.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.notices.deci: You are Ibrahim. What do you do?
Plan a weekend away — no phones.
Ibrahim planned a weekend away with no phones.
Start a small habit: ten minutes each evening, phones away, “tell me your day”.
Ibrahim started a ten-minute evening ritual.
Decide it’s a phase. Marriages have them.
Ibrahim decided it was just a phase.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.weekend.imag: Ibrahim and Sumayya walking a coastal path, no phones.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.weekend.pass: A weekend with no phones — whether planned or simply because the signal is bad at her parents’ village.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.weekend.less: Choose together; if you differ, talk it through and choose again.
content.adv-background-noise.scenes.weekend.deci: Together: what do you bring home from the weekend?
A daily ten minutes: phones down, “tell me your day”.
They brought home a daily ten minutes together.
A monthly evening out, just them.
They agreed a monthly evening out.
A lovely memory. Back to normal on Monday.
They came home with a lovely memory and changed nothing.
Ibrahim closing his book as Sumayya comes home.
A month later, Sumayya comes home with another funny story.
Close his book. “Go on — tell me.”
Ibrahim put everything down to hear her story.
Ibrahim half-listened while finishing an email.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.close.title: Close again
content.adv-background-noise.endings.close.image: Ibrahim and Sumayya laughing on the kitchen floor.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.close.whatH: Ten minutes a day became the best part of both their days.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.close.patte: Small, daily attention rebuilt what busyness had worn down.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.close.takea: Marriages rarely end in one fight. They fade from ignored small moments — and recover the same way.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.close.epilo: Asma says Sumayya seems happier. She is.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.close.guide: Ten minutes a day, phones down: “tell me about your day”.
Ibrahim and Sumayya doing separate things, back to back.
They are kind to each other and share very little. Sumayya’s best friend knows her better than her husband does.
Many small missed moments added up to distance without a single fight.
Pausing the match. Seeing the cake. Saying “tell me”.
No arguments does not mean no problems.
Sumayya has stopped trying to tell him things at all.
We turn toward each other’s small moments.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.alone.title: Alone together
content.adv-background-noise.endings.alone.image: Sumayya alone at the window at night.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.alone.whatH: Sumayya feels lonelier married than she ever did single.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.alone.patte: Presence in the same house is not the same as presence in someone’s life.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.alone.could: Ibrahim noticing; Sumayya saying it out loud.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.alone.takea: Loneliness inside a marriage is a warning, not a phase.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.alone.guide: If either of us feels alone, we say so — and the other stops everything.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.honest_cake: Ibrahim and Sumayya sharing cake at midnight.
The forgotten anniversary became the night they started really talking again.
He owned it; she said what it meant. The miss became a turning point.
Not forgetting — but the repair mattered more.
You will forget things. What matters is the repair.
When one of us forgets something important, we own it without excuses.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.dates.title: First Fridays
content.adv-background-noise.endings.dates.image: Ibrahim and Sumayya at their monthly dinner.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.dates.whatH: The first Friday of every month is theirs. The other days are still a bit busy.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.dates.patte: A protected monthly time helped, though daily attention still slips.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.dates.could: Small daily moments as well as monthly ones.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.dates.takea: Big gestures help; small daily ones matter more.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.dates.epilo: Some evenings Ibrahim still half-listens; Sumayya says so now.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.dates.guide: We keep a regular evening that belongs only to us.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.named.title: She said it out loud
content.adv-background-noise.endings.named.image: Ibrahim and Sumayya holding hands in a frank talk.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.named.whatH: Because Sumayya said “I feel unheard” before it became “I feel alone”, there was still time.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.named.patte: Naming the feeling early gave him the chance to change.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.named.takea: Say “I feel unheard” long before you feel alone.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.named.guide: We say when we feel unheard, before it grows.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.phase.title: Just a phase?
content.adv-background-noise.endings.phase.image: Ibrahim and Sumayya on their phones, close but apart.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.phase.whatH: It might have been a phase. It might be the start of a long drift. Neither can tell yet.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.phase.patte: Hoping distance resolves itself rarely works.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.phase.could: A small daily habit instead of waiting.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.phase.takea: Drift is the default. Closeness takes choosing.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.phase.guide: We choose each other on purpose, especially when life is busy.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.fine.title: Fine, mostly
Ibrahim and Sumayya washing up together.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.fine.whatHa: Not close, not distant. They have noticed the drift, which is more than most do.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.fine.patter: Awareness is the first step; habit is the second.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.fine.couldH: Turning the weekend into a lasting habit.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.fine.takeaw: Noticing the drift is good. Doing something small every day is better.
content.adv-background-noise.endings.fine.epilog: The loneliness is still there, quieter now.
We do one small thing for each other every day.
content.adv-starting-over.title: Starting Over at Thirty-Four
content.adv-starting-over.tagline: He wants to study the deen full-time. She would carry the bills for four years.
content.adv-starting-over.description: Musa wants to leave a secure job to study Islamic sciences full-time. It would mean Khadija carrying the household income for four years. Play both of them through a resignation letter, her parents’ reaction and a surprise that changes the maths — and find out what “supporting each other” really means.
content.adv-starting-over.cover.alt: A husband studying Arabic texts as his wife returns from work.
content.adv-starting-over.roles.A.name: Musa
content.adv-starting-over.roles.A.sketch: An engineer with a long-held dream of studying the deen properly.
content.adv-starting-over.roles.B.name: Khadija
content.adv-starting-over.roles.B.sketch: A senior nurse; proud of him, quietly worried about everything else.
They are deciding as one team.
content.adv-starting-over.variables.strain.label: Money strain
content.adv-starting-over.variables.strain.readi: Money is tight but talked about.
content.adv-starting-over.variables.fulfilment.r: Musa feels he gave up his calling.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.letter.title: The letter
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.letter.image.al: Musa reading his resignation letter at night.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.letter.passages: Musa has written his resignation letter. It has been sitting in his drafts for a week. He has not told Khadija it exists.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.letter.decision: You are Musa. What do you do?
Show Khadija the letter and ask what she thinks before sending anything.
Musa showed Khadija the letter before sending it.
Send it — he’s waited long enough.
Musa sent his resignation without telling Khadija.
A decision that moves your spouse’s life is not yours to make alone.
Musa dropped hints about his dream at dinner.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.her_reaction.im: Khadija reading the letter at the table.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.her_reaction.de: You are Khadija. What do you say?
“I’m proud of you. Let’s work out whether we can do this.”
Khadija said she was proud and wanted to work out if it was possible.
“I’m scared. Four years is a long time on one salary.”
Khadija said honestly that she was scared.
Khadija was angry that he decided without her.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.numbers.title: The spreadsheet
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.numbers.image.a: Musa and Khadija going through a budget.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.numbers.passage: They sit down with the numbers. It’s possible — just — if nothing goes wrong.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.numbers.decisio: What matters most to you here? Answer for yourself.
This is my calling. I’ll regret it forever if I don’t.
Musa said this was his calling.
I could study part-time and keep some work.
Musa offered to study part-time and keep some work.
Maybe it should wait a few years.
Musa wondered if it should wait.
I want to support him — with a safety net.
Khadija wanted to support him with a safety net.
I want children soon. How does this fit?
Khadija asked how children would fit.
I’ll carry it, whatever it costs me.
Khadija decided to carry it whatever it cost her.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.parents.title: Her parents hear
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.parents.image.a: Khadija’s parents reacting to the news.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.parents.passage: Khadija’s father is blunt: “A man provides. What is he thinking?”
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.parents.decisio: You are Khadija. What do you say to your father?
“We decided together. I believe in him.”
Khadija defended their decision to her father.
Say nothing — part of her agrees with him.
Khadija stayed quiet, half agreeing with her father.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.surprise.title: Two lines
Khadija looking at a pregnancy test.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.surprise.passag: Six weeks before term starts, Khadija is pregnant.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.surprise.decisi: Delay the studies a year and save.
They delayed the studies a year to save.
Musa studies part-time and keeps three days of work.
They chose part-time study with three days of work.
Go ahead as planned — they’ll find a way.
They went ahead with full-time study regardless.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.first_year.imag: Musa studying with the baby as Khadija leaves for a shift.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.first_year.pass: A year in. The baby is three months old.
Khadija is working nights again. She hasn’t said how tired she is.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.first_year.deci: You are Musa. What do you do?
Ask Khadija honestly how she’s coping — and mean it.
Musa asked Khadija honestly how she was coping.
Bury himself in study — it’s what they sacrificed for.
Khadija exhausted on the kitchen floor.
A night when the car breaks down, the rent is due and the baby won’t settle.
Sit down and talk honestly about whether this is working.
One of them asked to talk honestly about whether it was working.
Push through — it’s only one bad night.
One of them decided to push through.
Say what has been building up.
One of them said what had been building up.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.review.title: The review
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.review.image.al: Musa and Khadija reviewing their plan.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.review.passages: They sit down to decide what the next three years look like.
content.adv-starting-over.scenes.review.decision: Together: what’s the plan from here?
Continue, with clear help: family childcare two days, a budget they review monthly.
They continued with family help and a monthly budget review.
Musa pauses his studies and returns to work for a while.
Musa paused his studies and went back to work.
They pushed on exactly as before.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.shared_sacrifi: Musa graduating with Khadija and their child beside him.
Four years later, Musa graduates. Khadija is in the front row with their toddler. Both of them feel it was their degree.
Because they decided and adjusted together, the cost and the reward were both shared.
Little — though showing her the letter first saved them most of the pain.
Support your spouse’s calling with a plan, not just with faith.
Khadija’s father gives the first speech at the celebration.
We support each other’s dreams with a shared plan and regular reviews.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.burnout.title: Running on empty
Khadija asleep in a hospital break room.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.burnout.whatHa: Musa is thriving in his studies. Khadija is running on empty, and has stopped saying so.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.burnout.patter: One spouse’s dream was funded by the other’s silent exhaustion.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.burnout.couldH: Asking how she was coping — and adjusting when the answer was hard.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.burnout.takeaw: A calling that costs your spouse their health needs a new plan.
We check what our plans cost each other, honestly, every month.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.part_time.what: Part-time takes seven years instead of four. Nobody is exhausted, and nobody resents it.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.part_time.patt: Neither all-in nor giving up: a slower path everyone could live with.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.part_time.coul: Nothing — this was a good choice.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.part_time.take: The slower road is still a road.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.part_time.guid: When both options cost too much, we look for a slower third way.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.deferred.title: A dream deferred
content.adv-starting-over.endings.deferred.image: Musa at work, looking towards a distant minaret.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.deferred.whatH: Musa went back to engineering. He reads at night. He tells himself it is “for now”.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.deferred.patte: The family is secure; part of Musa is waiting.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.deferred.could: A part-time path might have kept the dream alive.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.deferred.takea: Deferring a dream is fine; forgetting it is not. Set a date to revisit.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.deferred.epilo: Khadija has started saving a little each month for his return to study.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.deferred.guide: When one of us defers a dream, we set a date to revisit it.
Khadija paying bills alone at night.
The studies go on. Khadija never quite forgets that the letter was sent before she saw it.
A shared life was changed by one person’s choice.
Ask before you leap — especially when your spouse will catch you.
We never make a life-changing decision without the other.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.father_was_rig: A tense family dinner with Khadija’s father.
Her father’s words hang over every money conversation. Khadija half-believes them now.
Unspoken agreement with a critic eroded the shared decision.
Khadija telling Musa about her doubts directly instead of letting them grow.
Bring doubts to your spouse before they become someone else’s argument.
We bring our doubts to each other first.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.partners.title: Partners
content.adv-starting-over.endings.partners.image: Musa studying and Khadija working, side by side.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.partners.whatH: Money is tight and nights are long. But every hard month is discussed, and every adjustment made together.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.partners.patte: They kept talking when it was hard, so hard never became hidden.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.partners.could: More help sooner would ease the load.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.partners.takea: Hard is survivable. Hidden is not.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.partners.guide: We talk about hard months as soon as they start.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.managing.title: Managing
content.adv-starting-over.endings.managing.image: An ordinary weekend at home for the family.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.managing.whatH: They are managing — some months better than others.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.managing.patte: The plan works, mostly, but has never been properly reviewed.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.managing.could: A regular review of how it is going for both of them.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.managing.takea: Review big plans regularly, not only when they break.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.managing.epilo: Money stress sits in the background of most evenings.
content.adv-starting-over.endings.managing.guide: We review big plans together every few months.
content.adv-the-brother.title: The Brother
content.adv-the-brother.tagline: Her brother is drowning in debt. She wants to help. He has doubts.
content.adv-the-brother.description: Naila’s younger brother Faisal is in serious debt and asks to borrow £8,000 — most of their savings. Naila wants to help; Hamid is not sure it will. Play both of them through the request, the loan (or not), the second request, and a family that thinks Hamid is heartless.
content.adv-the-brother.cover.alt: A brother asking his sister for help as her husband watches.
content.adv-the-brother.roles.A.name: Hamid
content.adv-the-brother.roles.A.sketch: Careful with money; likes Faisal but has seen this before.
content.adv-the-brother.roles.B.name: Naila
content.adv-the-brother.roles.B.sketch: Fiercely loyal to her family; the money is partly hers.
content.adv-the-brother.variables.family.label: Family ties
content.adv-the-brother.variables.family.reading: The family is strained but intact.
content.adv-the-brother.variables.trust.label: Trust about money
content.adv-the-brother.variables.trust.readings: Money is fully shared and trusted.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.request.title: The request
Faisal sits on their sofa and finally says it: he owes £8,000, the calls won’t stop, and he’s ashamed to ask.
You are Naila. What do you say to your brother?
“Let me talk to Hamid tonight. We’ll decide together.”
Naila told her brother she would decide with Hamid.
Naila promised her brother the money on the spot.
Promising shared money before asking your spouse makes them the villain if they hesitate.
Ask what the debt is for, and whether he has a plan.
Naila asked her brother what the debt was for and whether he had a plan.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.hamid_view.title: Hamid’s doubts
Hamid sharing his doubts with Naila.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.hamid_view.passag: That night, alone, Hamid shares his worry: Faisal borrowed from cousins last year and never paid it back.
Naila has already told Faisal yes.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.hamid_view.decisi: You are Hamid. How do you say it?
“I want to help him too. I just want to make sure it actually helps.”
Hamid said he wanted to help in a way that actually helped.
Say nothing and let Naila decide — it’s her brother.
Hamid stayed quiet and left it to Naila.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.decide.title: Deciding
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.decide.image.alt: Naila and Hamid deciding over their savings.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.decide.passages.0: £8,000 is most of their house deposit.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.decide.lessons.tb: Choose together; a mismatch means talk, then choose again.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.decide.decision.p: Together: what do you offer Faisal?
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.decide.decision.c: A loan with conditions: a debt advisor, a written repayment plan.
They offered a loan with conditions and a debt advisor.
A smaller gift they can afford to lose, plus help finding advice.
They gave a smaller gift and help finding advice.
They gave the full amount with no conditions.
No money — but they’ll help him find free debt advice.
They declined to lend but offered to help with advice.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.family_reacts.ima: Naila’s mother pleading on a video call.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.family_reacts.pas: “Your husband is heartless. Family helps family.”
“Thank you, my daughter. You saved him.”
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.family_reacts.dec: You are Naila. What do you say to your mother?
“Hamid and I decided this together, Mum.”
Naila told her mother it was a joint decision.
Naila told her mother it was Hamid’s idea.
Making your spouse the scapegoat with your family protects you today and costs you both for years.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.second_ask.title: Six months later
Naila reading another message from her brother.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.second_ask.passag: Six months later, a message from Faisal: “Sis, I hate to ask again…”
He is paying back the loan, slowly, through the advisor.
The £8,000 is gone. The debt is not.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.second_ask.decisi: What do you want to do?
Talk with Naila before anyone replies.
Hamid wanted to talk with Naila before replying.
Draw a line: no more money.
Hamid wanted to draw a firm line.
Send him a little from her own account, quietly.
Naila sent her brother money secretly.
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.reply.title: The reply
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.reply.image.alt: Naila and Hamid replying to Faisal together.
Hamid saw the transfer on the statement.
