content.adv-the-brother.scenes.reply.decision.pr: You are Hamid. What do you do?
content.adv-the-brother.scenes.reply.decision.ch: Offer Faisal their time instead: sit with him and go through his budget.
Hamid offered to sit with Faisal and go through his budget.
Hamid sent a kind but firm no.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.real_help.title: Real help
Faisal and Hamid going through his budget together.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.real_help.whatHa: Faisal is debt-free in eighteen months. He says the budget nights with Hamid saved him more than the money.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.real_help.patter: Conditions and time gave Faisal a way out, not just a bailout.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.real_help.takeaw: Sometimes the most loving help comes with conditions.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.real_help.epilog: Naila’s mother apologises to Hamid at Eid.
We help family together, in ways that actually help.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.united.title: United front
content.adv-the-brother.endings.united.image.alt: Naila and Hamid standing together at a family gathering.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.united.whatHappe: The family was angry for a while. Naila never once let them blame Hamid.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.united.pattern.e: Standing together turned a family conflict into a test they passed.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.united.couldHave: A softer answer to the family might have kept more warmth.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.united.takeaway: Disagree in private; stand together in public.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.united.guide.tb-: We never let family blame one of us for a decision we made together.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.bottomless.title: A bottomless well
content.adv-the-brother.endings.bottomless.image: Naila and Hamid looking at an empty savings jar.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.bottomless.whatH: The deposit is gone. Faisal still owes money. The requests keep coming.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.bottomless.patte: Money without conditions solved the symptom and fed the cause.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.bottomless.could: A debt advisor and a written plan before any money moved.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.bottomless.takea: Rescuing someone who is drowning often means teaching them to swim.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.bottomless.guide: Large loans to family come with a plan and our joint agreement.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.secret.title: The secret transfer
content.adv-the-brother.endings.secret.image.alt: Hamid holding a bank statement, hurt.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.secret.whatHappe: The amount was small. The secret was not. It takes Hamid a long time to stop checking statements.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.secret.pattern.e: Hidden money broke more trust than any loan could cost.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.secret.takeaway: Hidden money is a hidden wound.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.secret.guide.tb-: No secret money between us — ever.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.scapegoat.title: The villain
Hamid sitting alone at a family gathering.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.scapegoat.whatHa: Her family treats Hamid like an outsider. He no longer goes to family dinners.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.scapegoat.patter: Blaming him protected her standing and isolated him.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.scapegoat.takeaw: Your family will follow your lead on how to treat your spouse.
We show our families how to treat each other.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.generous.title: Generosity, with limits
content.adv-the-brother.endings.generous.image.a: Naila giving Faisal an envelope at the door.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.generous.whatHap: The gift helped a little. The advice helped more. The deposit is intact.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.generous.pattern: Giving what you can afford to lose
A gift with no strings, sized to what they could lose, kept everyone safe.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.generous.takeawa: Give to family what you can afford to lose, not what you cannot.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.generous.guide.t: We give to family what we can afford to lose.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.cold_family.imag: Naila looking at a quiet family chat.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.cold_family.what: They protected their future, and their family went quiet for a year.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.cold_family.patt: The right boundary, delivered without warmth, cost them closeness.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.cold_family.coul: Offering time and advice alongside the no.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.cold_family.take: A no lands better with a yes to something else.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.cold_family.guid: When we say no to family, we offer something else too.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.working_out.imag: Naila and Hamid walking home from a family dinner.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.working_out.what: Faisal is still struggling. They are still working out how much is theirs to fix.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.working_out.patt: They have not yet agreed what “helping family” means for them.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.working_out.coul: Agreeing their limits before the first request.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.working_out.take: Agree your family-money limits before someone asks.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.working_out.epil: Money conversations still feel tense between them.
content.adv-the-brother.endings.working_out.guid: We agree our limits for family money in advance.
content.adv-whose-wedding.title: Whose Wedding Is It?
content.adv-whose-wedding.tagline: They want a small nikah. Both mothers want five hundred guests.
content.adv-whose-wedding.description: Adam and Mariam want a small, simple nikah and to put their savings toward a home. Both mothers are planning a wedding for five hundred. Play both of them through a deposit paid without asking, a disagreement between the two of you, and an elder who offers to help — and find out whose day it turns into.
content.adv-whose-wedding.cover.alt: An engaged couple buried in wedding plans as both mothers talk on phones.
content.adv-whose-wedding.roles.A.name: Adam
content.adv-whose-wedding.roles.A.sketch: Easygoing; hates conflict with his mother.
content.adv-whose-wedding.roles.B.name: Mariam
content.adv-whose-wedding.roles.B.sketch: Organised; dreams of a small nikah and a home of their own.
They are pulled apart by their families.
content.adv-whose-wedding.variables.family.label: Family goodwill
content.adv-whose-wedding.variables.debt.label: Wedding debt
content.adv-whose-wedding.variables.debt.reading: The wedding has put them in debt.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.deposit.title: The deposit
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.deposit.image.a: Mariam seeing a hall booking confirmation.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.deposit.passage: Adam’s mother has paid a deposit on a 500-seat hall. Mariam finds out from the hall’s confirmation email, which lists Adam as the contact.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.deposit.decisio: You are Adam. Mariam is looking at you. What do you say?
“I knew she was looking, and I didn’t stop her. I’m sorry. Let’s decide together.”
Adam admitted he knew and asked to decide together.
“She did it herself — you know what she’s like.”
“She just wants it to be special for us.”
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.mothers.title: Two mothers, one guest list
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.mothers.image.a: Both mothers holding up long guest lists on a call.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.mothers.passage: Mariam’s mother, not to be outdone, has started a guest list of her own. It’s at 280 and climbing.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.mothers.decisio: You are Mariam. What do you do?
Ask Adam to sit down and agree, just the two of you, what you actually want.
Mariam asked Adam to agree what they wanted, just the two of them.
Ask her own mother to back off.
Mariam asked her own mother to back off.
Let them get on with it. It’s easier.
Mariam let the mothers take over.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.us.title: What do we want?
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.us.image.alt: Adam and Mariam writing privately, back to back.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.us.passages.0.t: Back to back, each writes down what they actually want the wedding to be.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.us.decision.byR: Small, simple, and money toward a home.
Adam wrote: small, simple, money toward a home.
Adam wrote: whatever keeps his mother happy.
A small nikah, then a bigger celebration later.
Adam wrote: a small nikah, a bigger celebration later.
Small, simple, and money toward a home.
Mariam wrote: small, simple, money toward a home.
Meaningful — the guest count matters less than who’s there.
Mariam wrote: I don’t mind any more.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.elder.title: An elder offers
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.elder.image.alt: An elder listening to Adam and Mariam.
Mariam’s grandfather, respected by both families, offers to help. “Tell me what you two want, and I will speak to your mothers.”
Together: what do you ask him to say?
A small nikah at the masjid, a modest walimah, savings to a home.
They asked for a small nikah and modest walimah.
A small nikah now; a bigger family celebration in a year.
They asked for a small nikah now and a celebration later.
Let the mothers have the big wedding — but split the cost three ways.
They agreed to the big wedding with costs shared.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.mothers_hear.im: Both mothers listening to the grandfather.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.mothers_hear.pa: The grandfather speaks to both mothers. Adam’s mother is quiet. Then she turns to Adam: “Is this what you want?”
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.mothers_hear.de: You are Adam. What do you say to your mother?
“Yes, Mum. It’s what we both want. Will you help us make it beautiful?”
Adam told his mother it was what they both wanted and asked for her help.
Adam wavered in front of his mother.
Agreeing as a couple and then wavering in front of a parent undoes the agreement.
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.costs.title: The costs
content.adv-whose-wedding.scenes.costs.image.alt: Adam and Mariam going over wedding costs.
The 500-seat hall alone would take most of their home savings.
You are Mariam. What do you do?
Set a firm budget and tell both families: this is the limit.
Mariam set a firm budget and told both families.
Take a loan to cover the gap. It’s once in a lifetime.
They took a loan to cover the wedding.
Trim what they can and accept the rest.
They trimmed what they could and accepted the rest.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.their_day.imag: A small nikah with close family.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.their_day.what: Thirty people, a masjid, a garden walimah — and a deposit on a flat the week after.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.their_day.patt: They agreed first, then spoke to their families with one voice.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.their_day.coul: Agreeing before the hall was ever booked.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.their_day.take: Decide together first; then tell your families together.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.their_day.epil: Adam’s mother says it was the most beautiful wedding she has been to.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.their_day.guid: We agree between ourselves before we answer our families.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.two_days.title: Two celebrations
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.two_days.image: A family celebration a year after the nikah.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.two_days.whatH: A quiet nikah now; a joyful family party a year later, paid for without debt.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.two_days.patte: Splitting the day gave everyone what mattered most to them.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.two_days.takea: When you can’t agree on one thing, consider two.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.two_days.guide: When we are stuck, we look for a way both sides get what matters most.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.big_day.title: Five hundred guests
A huge wedding hall full of guests.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.big_day.whatHa: It is the wedding their mothers dreamed of. It is lovely. They are exhausted.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.big_day.patter: They chose family joy over their own preference — and shared the cost fairly.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.big_day.couldH: Nothing wrong with it, as long as it was a real choice.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.big_day.takeaw: Giving your families their day is a gift — if you choose it together.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.big_day.epilog: The shared costs mean nobody starts married in debt.
If we give family what they want, it is a choice we make together.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.debt.title: The wedding loan
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.debt.image.alt: Adam and Mariam looking at a loan statement.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.debt.whatHappe: The wedding was beautiful. The loan will take four years to pay off. The flat will wait.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.debt.pattern.e: One day was paid for with years of their shared future.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.debt.couldHave: A firm budget, set together, before the quotes came in.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.debt.takeaway: Don’t borrow your future to impress a crowd.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.debt.guide.ww-: We do not take on debt for celebrations.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.wavered.title: “Whatever you think”
Mariam watching Adam with his mother at the wedding.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.wavered.whatHa: The wedding happened his mother’s way. Mariam remembers the moment Adam said “whatever you think”.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.wavered.patter: A couple’s agreement collapsed the moment it was tested by a parent.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.wavered.couldH: “Yes, Mum. It’s what we both want.”
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.wavered.takeaw: Your spouse is watching whose side you stand on — even at the wedding.
Once we agree, we stand by it in front of family.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.handed_over.im: The mothers running the hall while the couple sit aside.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.handed_over.wh: They let the mothers plan everything. It was a lovely party. It didn’t feel like theirs.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.handed_over.pa: Avoiding conflict meant their own wishes were never spoken.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.handed_over.co: Writing down, and saying, what they each wanted.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.handed_over.ta: Avoiding a conversation is also a decision.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.handed_over.gu: We say what we want, even when it is easier not to.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.tense_families: Two families sitting stiffly apart at the wedding.
The small wedding went ahead. Both mothers felt shut out, and said so for a year.
The right decision was delivered in a way that left the mothers feeling dismissed.
Inviting the mothers to help make the small day beautiful.
Include family in how, even when you decide what.
We include family in how we celebrate, even when we decide what.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.good_enough.im: A medium-sized wedding in a community hall.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.good_enough.wh: A medium wedding, a medium budget, medium frustration. Married, and that is what matters.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.good_enough.pa: Nobody got exactly what they wanted, and the marriage started intact.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.good_enough.co: A clearer plan earlier would have spared the stress.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.good_enough.ta: The wedding lasts a day; how you made it together lasts longer.
content.adv-whose-wedding.endings.good_enough.gu: We remember that the marriage matters more than the wedding.
content.adv-long-way.title: A Long Way from the Masjid
content.adv-long-way.tagline: A new job, a small town, no masjid. One of them thrives; one feels lost.
content.adv-long-way.description: Yusuf takes a job in a small coastal town. No masjid, no halal butcher, no Muslim friends. He loves the quiet; Hafsa feels like she has lost her whole world. Play both of them through a first lonely Eid, a front-room prayer that grows, and an offer to move back.
content.adv-long-way.cover.alt: A couple outside a countryside cottage, one excited, one uncertain.
content.adv-long-way.roles.A.name: Yusuf
content.adv-long-way.roles.A.sketch: Loves his new job and the slower pace; busy all day.
content.adv-long-way.roles.B.name: Hafsa
content.adv-long-way.roles.B.sketch: Left her family, her halaqa and her friends behind; works remotely, alone.
content.adv-long-way.variables.belonging.label: Belonging
content.adv-long-way.variables.belonging.reading: Hafsa feels like a stranger here.
This place is starting to feel like home.
content.adv-long-way.variables.closeness.label: Closeness
content.adv-long-way.variables.closeness.reading: The move has brought them closer.
content.adv-long-way.variables.faith.label: Faith life
content.adv-long-way.variables.faith.readings.0: Their faith feels thin out here.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.arrival.title: Three weeks in
content.adv-long-way.scenes.arrival.image.alt: Hafsa alone at the window of the cottage.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.arrival.passages.0.t: Three weeks in. Yusuf comes home buzzing about his team. Hafsa has not spoken to another person all day.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.arrival.decision.pro: You are Yusuf. How do you greet her?
content.adv-long-way.scenes.arrival.decision.cho: Ask about her day first — really ask.
Yusuf asked about Hafsa’s day before telling her about his.
Tell her all about his great day.
Yusuf told Hafsa all about his great day.
“You’ll love it once you settle in!”
Yusuf told her she’d love it once she settled in.
Reassurance before understanding can feel like being told your feelings are wrong.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.her_day.title: The truth
content.adv-long-way.scenes.her_day.image.alt: Hafsa telling Yusuf how lonely she is.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.her_day.passages.0.t: Hafsa decides whether to say how she really feels.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.her_day.decision.pro: You are Hafsa. What do you say?
content.adv-long-way.scenes.her_day.decision.cho: “I’m really lonely here. I need us to do something about it.”
Hafsa told Yusuf honestly that she was lonely.
Hafsa said it was just an adjustment.
Hafsa said she wished they had never moved.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.eid.title: The first Eid alone
content.adv-long-way.scenes.eid.image.alt: Yusuf and Hafsa praying Eid alone, family on a video call.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.eid.passages.0.text: Eid morning. The nearest masjid is ninety minutes away. Their families are on a video call, eating together.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.eid.passages.1.text: Hafsa has been saying it’s fine for weeks. It is not fine.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.eid.decision.prompt: What do you want to do today?
Drive ninety minutes to the city masjid for Eid prayer.
Yusuf wanted to drive to the city masjid for Eid.
Make Eid special at home, just the two of them.
Yusuf wanted to make Eid special at home.
Pop into work for a couple of hours — it’s a busy week.
Yusuf went into work for a few hours on Eid.
Drive to the city masjid, whatever it takes.
Hafsa wanted to drive to the city masjid.
Invite the one friendly neighbour round for Eid sweets.
Hafsa invited their friendly neighbour for Eid sweets.
Spend the morning on the video call, crying.
Hafsa spent the morning on the call with family, crying.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.front_room.title: The front room
content.adv-long-way.scenes.front_room.image.alt: A small group praying in the couple’s front room.
Hafsa has an idea: a weekly gathering in their front room for the handful of Muslims within an hour’s drive.
The families they met at the city masjid would come.
Start it — Friday evenings, food and a short talk.
They started a Friday-evening gathering at home.
They decided they were too tired to start anything yet.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.offer.title: An offer to move back
content.adv-long-way.scenes.offer.image.alt: Yusuf reading a job offer back in the city.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.offer.passages.0.tex: A year in, Yusuf is offered a role back in the city, near both families.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.offer.passages.1.tex: The Friday gathering now has fourteen regulars. Hafsa is the one who organises it.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.offer.decision.choic: One of them wanted to stay.
Go back. Family and community matter more.
One of them wanted to go back.
One of them was unsure and wanted to talk.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.decide.title: Deciding
content.adv-long-way.scenes.decide.image.alt: Yusuf and Hafsa deciding on the sea wall.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.decide.passages.0.te: They sit on the sea wall and decide.
content.adv-long-way.scenes.decide.decision.choi: Stay — and keep building what they started.
Move back to the city, near family.
They chose to move back to the city.
content.adv-long-way.endings.built_community.ima: A small community gathering the couple built.
content.adv-long-way.endings.built_community.wha: Three years on, the Friday gathering has a rented hall. Hafsa runs the women’s circle. She calls the town home.
content.adv-long-way.endings.built_community.pat: Instead of waiting for belonging, they created it together.
content.adv-long-way.endings.built_community.cou: Nothing — though saying “I’m lonely” on day one sped everything up.
content.adv-long-way.endings.built_community.tak: If you can’t find the community you need, you may be meant to start it.
content.adv-long-way.endings.built_community.epi: Their old neighbour comes to every Eid now.
content.adv-long-way.endings.built_community.gui: Wherever we live, we build a community around our home.
content.adv-long-way.endings.home_again.title: Home, changed
content.adv-long-way.endings.home_again.image.al: Yusuf and Hafsa arriving home to their families.
content.adv-long-way.endings.home_again.whatHapp: They move back. They are closer than when they left — they learned to rely on each other out there.
Isolation, faced together, deepened the marriage.
content.adv-long-way.endings.home_again.takeaway: A hard season faced together is never wasted.
content.adv-long-way.endings.home_again.guide.lw: We face hard seasons as a team, wherever we are.
content.adv-long-way.endings.lonely_stay.title: Staying for him
content.adv-long-way.endings.lonely_stay.image.a: Hafsa alone on a winter beach.
content.adv-long-way.endings.lonely_stay.whatHap: They stayed because Yusuf loved it. Hafsa is still lonely, and has stopped mentioning it.
content.adv-long-way.endings.lonely_stay.pattern: The move suited one spouse and quietly diminished the other.
content.adv-long-way.endings.lonely_stay.couldHa: Taking her loneliness as seriously as his job.
content.adv-long-way.endings.lonely_stay.takeawa: A move is right only if it is right for both of you.
content.adv-long-way.endings.lonely_stay.guide.l: Where we live has to work for both of us.
content.adv-long-way.endings.two_lives.title: Two different lives
content.adv-long-way.endings.two_lives.image.alt: Yusuf leaving as Hafsa stays on a family video call.
content.adv-long-way.endings.two_lives.whatHappe: Yusuf’s life is the job and the coast. Hafsa’s life is the video calls home. They share a house.
content.adv-long-way.endings.two_lives.pattern.e: Each coped alone, and the coping drew them apart.
content.adv-long-way.endings.two_lives.couldHave: Starting something together — the gathering, a routine, anything shared.
content.adv-long-way.endings.two_lives.takeaway: In a new place, build at least one thing together.
content.adv-long-way.endings.two_lives.guide.lw-: In a new place, we build at least one thing together.
content.adv-long-way.endings.deeper_faith.title: A quieter faith
Yusuf and Hafsa praying Fajr by the sea.
content.adv-long-way.endings.deeper_faith.whatHa: No masjid, no community — and their own faith, practised together at home, has never been stronger.
content.adv-long-way.endings.deeper_faith.patter: Without outside structure, they made worship their own shared habit.
content.adv-long-way.endings.deeper_faith.takeaw: The home can be a masjid too.
We keep worship alive at home, together.
content.adv-long-way.endings.regret.title: Moving back, unhealed
content.adv-long-way.endings.regret.image.alt: Yusuf and Hafsa driving back to the city in silence.
content.adv-long-way.endings.regret.whatHappened: They move back. Yusuf misses the coast; Hafsa never quite forgives the year.
content.adv-long-way.endings.regret.pattern.name: Unprocessed hurt
content.adv-long-way.endings.regret.pattern.expl: The loneliness was escaped, never talked through.
content.adv-long-way.endings.regret.couldHaveCha: Talking about what the year cost each of them.
content.adv-long-way.endings.regret.takeaway: Leaving a hard place does not heal what happened there. Talking does.
content.adv-long-way.endings.regret.guide.lw-e-t: After a hard season, we talk about what it cost each of us.
content.adv-long-way.endings.getting_there.title: Getting there
content.adv-long-way.endings.getting_there.image: Yusuf and Hafsa chatting with a neighbour on the seafront.
content.adv-long-way.endings.getting_there.whatH: Not home yet, but not a stranger’s town any more either.
content.adv-long-way.endings.getting_there.patte: Belonging grows slowly, and they kept at it.
content.adv-long-way.endings.getting_there.takea: Belonging is built a little each week.
content.adv-long-way.endings.getting_there.epilo: The online halaqa has become a lifeline for Hafsa.
content.adv-long-way.endings.getting_there.guide: We do one thing each week to belong where we live.
content.adv-long-way.endings.honest_return.title: An honest return
content.adv-long-way.endings.honest_return.image: Yusuf and Hafsa hanging a photo of the sea in their city flat.
content.adv-long-way.endings.honest_return.whatH: They decide together to go back. The sea photo goes on the wall of their new flat.
content.adv-long-way.endings.honest_return.patte: They weighed both their needs and chose together.
content.adv-long-way.endings.honest_return.takea: Changing your mind together is not failure.
content.adv-long-way.endings.honest_return.guide: We can change our minds, as long as we decide together.
content.adv-raised-voice.title: The Raised Voice
content.adv-raised-voice.tagline: In his home, shouting meant nothing. In hers, it meant everything.
content.adv-raised-voice.description: Adnan grew up in a loud, loving house where everyone shouted and nobody held a grudge. Huda grew up in a quiet house where a raised voice meant something was badly wrong. Their first real argument goes badly. Play both of them through a slammed door, an apology that doesn’t land, and a conversation about the homes they came from.
content.adv-raised-voice.cover.alt: A couple on opposite sides of a kitchen after an argument.
content.adv-raised-voice.roles.A.name: Adnan
content.adv-raised-voice.roles.A.sketch: Warm, loud, quick to anger and quick to forget.
content.adv-raised-voice.roles.B.name: Huda
content.adv-raised-voice.roles.B.sketch: Calm, careful; goes very still when voices rise.
content.adv-raised-voice.variables.safety.label: Feeling safe
content.adv-raised-voice.variables.understanding: They are starting to understand each other.
They understand where each other comes from.
content.adv-raised-voice.variables.repair.label: Repair
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.argument.title: The argument
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.argument.image.a: Adnan raising his voice as Huda goes still.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.argument.passage: It starts about the car keys and turns into everything. Adnan’s voice gets louder. A plate slips and smashes. Huda goes completely silent.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.argument.decisio: You are Adnan. What do you do?
Stop mid-sentence. “I’m shouting. I’m sorry. Let me calm down.”
Adnan stopped himself mid-shout and apologised.
Keep going — he’s not done, and he’s not angry with her, really.
Storm out and slam the door.
Adnan stormed out and slammed the door.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.after.title: Afterwards
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.after.image.alt: Huda alone on the edge of the bed after the argument.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.after.passages.0: Huda is shaking. For her, a raised voice has only ever meant something was terribly wrong.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.after.passages.1: The slammed door is still echoing.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.after.decision.p: You are Huda. What do you do?
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.after.decision.c: Later, tell Adnan: “When you shout, I feel scared — even if you don’t mean it.”
Huda told Adnan that shouting scared her.
Say nothing. Be very careful around him for days.
Huda went quiet and careful for days.
Call her mother and stay there for the night.
Huda went to her mother’s for the night.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.apology.title: The apology
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.apology.image.al: Adnan offering flowers that don’t quite land.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.apology.passages: Adnan comes to apologise. In his family, you apologise, hug, and it’s over.
She is at her mother’s. He has to go and knock on her parents’ door.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.apology.decision: “Sorry about earlier — we’re good, yeah?” and a hug.
Adnan apologised quickly and went for a hug.
“I’m sorry. Can you tell me what it was like for you?”
Adnan apologised and asked what it had been like for her.
Explain that shouting is normal in his family; she shouldn’t take it personally.
Adnan explained that shouting was normal in his family.
Accept it to make it stop.
Huda accepted the apology to make it stop.
Explain what a raised voice meant in her house.
Huda explained what a raised voice meant in her home.
Huda said she was not ready yet.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.homes.title: The homes we came from
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.homes.image.alt: Adnan and Huda looking at childhood photos together.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.homes.passages.0: A week later, they talk about the homes they each grew up in — the loud one and the quiet one.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.homes.lessons.rv: Choose together. If you differ, talk it through and choose again.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.homes.decision.p: Together: what will you agree for arguments?
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.homes.decision.c: A signal: either says “pause”, and they take twenty minutes apart, then come back.
They agreed a pause signal and a twenty-minute break.
No raised voices, ever — whatever the topic.
They agreed no raised voices, ever.
Nothing formal — they’ll just try harder.
They agreed to just try harder.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.second.title: The second argument
A month later, another argument — about his sister staying for two weeks. Adnan feels his voice starting to rise.
You are Adnan. What do you do?
“Pause.” Walk to the kitchen, make tea, come back in twenty minutes.
Adnan called a pause and came back calmer.
Notice, and deliberately lower his voice.
Adnan noticed and lowered his voice.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.huda_turn.title: Huda’s side
Huda speaking firmly across the table.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.huda_turn.passag: Huda has her own part to play: in her home, people went silent for days instead of shouting.
He shouted again. She has gone quiet for three days.
content.adv-raised-voice.scenes.huda_turn.decisi: You are Huda. What do you do?
Say what she needs instead of going silent.
Huda said what she needed instead of going silent.
Go silent — it’s how her family handled it.
Huda went silent, the way her family always had.
Suggest they see a counsellor together.
Huda suggested seeing a counsellor together.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.fight_fair.imag: Adnan and Huda calling a pause with a smile.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.fight_fair.what: “Pause” has become a family word. Arguments still happen; nobody is frightened by them.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.fight_fair.patt: They built a signal that worked for both their histories.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.fight_fair.coul: Little — though talking about their childhood homes before the wedding would have helped.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.fight_fair.take: Every couple fights. Couples who last agree how.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.fight_fair.epil: Adnan’s loud family have started using “pause” too.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.fight_fair.guid: Either of us can say “pause”; we take twenty minutes and come back.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.understood.what: The night he asked “what was it like for you?” changed how Adnan argues.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.understood.patt: Seeing the other’s reaction as their history, not an attack, changed everything.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.understood.take: Behind every strong reaction is a home someone grew up in.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.understood.guid: When one of us reacts strongly, we ask about where it comes from.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.eggshells.title: Walking on eggshells
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.eggshells.whatH: Adnan rarely shouts now. Huda still braces whenever he sighs.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.eggshells.patte: The shouting stopped; the fear was never talked through.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.eggshells.could: An apology that asked how she felt, not just one that said sorry.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.eggshells.takea: Stopping the behaviour is not the same as healing the hurt.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.eggshells.guide: After we hurt each other, we talk about it until it is healed.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.repeating.title: It happens again
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.repeating.image: Adnan and Huda not speaking on opposite ends of the sofa.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.repeating.whatH: The loud arguments and the long silences keep alternating. Each makes the other worse.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.repeating.patte: His shouting triggered her silence; her silence fed his frustration.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.repeating.could: A pause signal — and both naming their pattern.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.repeating.takea: His loud and her quiet are two halves of one pattern. Change it together.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.repeating.guide: We name our conflict pattern out loud and work on it together.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.counsel.title: Asking for help
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.counsel.image.a: Adnan and Huda with a counsellor.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.counsel.whatHap: They start seeing a Muslim counsellor together. It is the best decision of their first year.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.counsel.pattern: They treated a pattern as something to learn about, not something shameful.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.counsel.couldHa: Nothing — asking for help was strength.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.counsel.takeawa: Getting help early is a sign of how much you care.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.counsel.guide.r: We are not too proud to get help with our marriage.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.papered.title: Papered over
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.papered.image.a: Adnan and Huda smiling in a photo with a cracked frame.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.papered.whatHap: A quick sorry and a hug every time. It feels fine until the next one.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.papered.pattern: Fast apologies skipped the part where they understood each other.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.papered.couldHa: Asking “what was it like for you?”
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.papered.takeawa: A quick sorry ends the fight. Understanding ends the pattern.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.papered.guide.r: Our apologies include asking how the other felt.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.learning.title: Learning each other
Adnan and Huda washing dishes together.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.learning.whatHa: Some arguments go better than others. They are learning each other’s signals.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.learning.patter: Different homes meant different rules; they are writing new ones.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.learning.couldH: An agreed signal would speed things up.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.learning.takeaw: You both bring a family’s rules into marriage. Write your own together.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.learning.epilog: Huda still goes quiet sometimes; Adnan has learned to notice.
We write our own rules for disagreeing, not our parents’.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.quiet_rule.imag: Adnan and Huda reading in a quiet living room.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.quiet_rule.what: No raised voices, ever. It’s peaceful. Sometimes Adnan feels he can’t be himself at home.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.quiet_rule.patt: The rule protected Huda but asked Adnan to hide something real.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.quiet_rule.coul: A rule that worked for both of them, like a pause signal.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.quiet_rule.take: A good rule protects both people, not just one.
content.adv-raised-voice.endings.quiet_rule.guid: Our rules for conflict have to work for both of us.
